name: Deal ticket and transport contract set-up
definition: Creating, extending or replacing deal tickets and transport contracts in Sitara so that gas at a meter or on a pipeline has a valid deal for the month.

synthesis.description: A round usually starts when a scheduler, volume analyst or accountant finds gas flowing at a meter or on a pipeline with no valid deal: a ticket expired, ended mid-month or was never created. They email the desk, mostly Daren Farmer, asking for a Sitara deal to be created, extended, zeroed out or corrected. The desk or a logistics coordinator enters or extends the ticket and replies with the deal or track number. The requester then checks that the ticket reflects the flow, so that allocations and the Unify volume drafts can clear.
steps: A scheduler or analyst finds flow at a meter with no deal, an expired ticket or an allocation exception.
They email the desk with the meter, dates, counterparty and any existing deal number.
The desk checks Sitara to see whether the existing deal should be extended or a new one created.
The trader or coordinator creates, extends, zeroes or corrects the ticket in Sitara.
The deal or track number is sent back to the requester.
The requester confirms the ticket is released and flows into Unify so allocations and volume drafts can clear.
stalls: Requesters wait on the desk to enter or release a deal and have to ask again; logistics stays blocked until the trader answers.
Expired or unreleased tickets stop deals from passing into Unify, so volumes cannot be drafted until the ticket is fixed.
Requesters are unsure who can make the change, and requests are passed between people or redirected to another person.
Deal terms are sent with mistakes in the effective date or price and have to be corrected after the first request.
contradictions: Different people are named as the one who puts these deals in: an outside party is told to call Daren Farmer, while another sender says Danny Conner handles it and a third says to talk to Darren.
In the same round, setting up the accounting arrangements is assigned to Volume Management as a group, while Robert E Lloyd splits the months between himself and a colleague.
synthesis.approach: A daily exception report comparing measured flow and allocation exceptions by meter against active Sitara tickets would flag meters with flow but no deal, and tickets expiring before month end, before anyone has to email. A standard request form would capture meter, dates, counterparty, price and existing deal number, and route to the named owner for that pipeline, with the new deal number returned automatically.
synthesis.rationale: Most rounds are the same request missing the same fields (meter, dates, deal number, extend or create), and many stall on who handles it. A structured request form with a routing owner column removes the back-and-forth and the incorrect terms, while the trader still decides whether to extend or create.

estimate.label: estimate, not a count
estimate.rationale: The requester looks up the meter, flow dates and expired ticket; the desk checks Sitara for the existing deal, decides extend or create, enters or corrects the ticket and confirms it reaches Unify. A simple extension takes about 10 minutes; multi-ticket clean-ups and replacement deals take longer, hence the mid of 20. Detection of missing deals and the request fields can be automated; the trading decision and entry review stay manual.
